The Opportunity As a dedicated Property Adjuster Specialist , you will work within established guidelines and framework to investigate, evaluate, negotiate, and settle complex property insurance claims presented by or against our members. You will confirm and analyzes coverage, recognize liability exposure and negotiate equitable settlements in compliance with all state regulatory requirements. Property Adjuster Specialist focus on using technology and desk adjusting for a virtual first approach to inspections and claims handling. USAA also provides a company vehicle to physically inspect losses within your locally assigned territory. Field Adjusters may travel outside of their local territory to respond to claims in other regions when needed. This is an hourly, non-exempt position with paid overtime available. This is a field-based role for The Woodlands, TX . Candidates currently living in this location or willing to self-relocate are encouraged to apply. Partners with vendors and internal business partners to facilitate complex claims resolution. May also involve external regulatory coordination to ensure appropriate documentation and compliance. Investigates claim damages by conducting research from various sources, including the insured, third parties, and external resources. May identify and resolve potential discrepancies and identifies subrogation potential resulting from unusual characteristics. Identifies coverage concerns, reviews prior loss history, determines and creates Special Investigation Unit (SIU) referrals, when appropriate. Job Description At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features. Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale. The Role The Manufacturing Execution Engineer GA for ME Optimization is responsible for leading General Assembly manufacturing optimization projects across multiple assembly sites. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams across Manufacturing Engineering, Plant Production, Industrial Engineering, Quality, and Maintenance to design, build, and commission state-of-the-art automation in GM vehicle assembly plants. This role plays a key part in shaping how General Motors operates within General Assembly and advancing our journey toward the factory of the future. You will be accountable for maximizing efficiency and reducing MCPU through effective utilization of personnel, materials, equipment, and facilities. Key deliverables include leading the coordination, planning, budgeting, development, and execution of GA optimization projects from ideation through installation, and creating efficient, lean processes that can be deployed across the GM enterprise. Work is performed in a centralized manufacturing engineering environment as well as in assembly plants, with a high level of independent judgment and interaction with all levels of the organization. What You'll Do (Responsibilities) Define all areas of change, including product and manufacturing requirements (tooling, automation, workstation layout, facilities, etc.). Analyze and design efficient material flow and future-state material movement strategies. Develop interfaces and work with cross-functional teams to define and deploy common tooling, processes, and standards across the department and enterprise. Provide technical direction to, and oversight of, outside vendors and internal product/plant teams. Lead the design, construction, integration, plant installation, launch, and continuous improvement of equipment and tools required to produce high-quality vehicles. Lead coordination of automation projects, including all plant integration and pull-ahead activities with Continuous Improvement leads and Plant ME/IE teams. Coordinate transparent, aligned project validation metrics driven by design capability and simulated site throughput standards. Apply strong analytical and problem-solving skills to resolve complex, unusual issues in manufacturing and automation. Utilize deep technical knowledge of automated processes to identify, evaluate, and implement optimization opportunities. Conduct project plan reviews with local production management for future implementations, including understanding local contractual considerations. Provide technical support and assistance to manufacturing and maintenance team members, production supervisors, and production associates. Ensure projects meet financial and budget targets, tracking costs and savings against objectives. Quickly interpret plant layouts and propose General Assembly automation concepts, tooling solutions, and integration approaches. Maintain a strong understanding of Bill of Process (BOP) and Bill of Equipment (BOE) and their application in GA optimization. Manage timing, resources, budget, lessons learned, performance scorecards, meeting minutes, and weekly one-page project status reports for all assigned projects. Support vehicle performance integration, driving design solutions to integration issues impacting General Assembly. Own engineering deliverable status for Program Execution Teams and Program Quality Readiness Reviews. Provide engineering launch leadership, including on-site support at assembly plant launches.
